ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Sigmund Freud Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: Establishing primary care seven years after maxillectomy for palatal cancer: about twenty cigars a day, a worn obturator, pain and weight loss. Concerns: He doubts he can work without cigars and has failed to stop many times; His obturator leaks and rubs, which makes speaking, eating and working harder; He fears the cancer coming back. [S]

One tablet twice daily after food
Nicotine 21 mg/24 hours transdermal patch, one patch each morning from the quit date, for six weeks

Nicotine 4 mg oral lozenge, one lozenge as needed for cravings, up to 10 a day, dissolved on the side away from the obturator; gum avoided because it sticks to the prosthesis
One lozenge as needed, up to 10 a day
Acetaminophen 500 mg oral tablet, two tablets three times daily (3,000 mg a day) for pain at the maxillectomy site
Nystatin 100,000 units/mL oral suspension, 5 mL swished around the mouth and defect for as long as possible and then swallowed, four times daily with the obturator out, for 14 days
5 mL four times daily for 14 days
Atorvastatin 20 mg oral tablet, one tablet daily

tr.td: Establishing primary care seven years after maxillectomy for palatal cancer: about twenty cigars a day, a worn obturator, pain and weight loss
Two-week review with the maxillofacial prosthodontics consultation: obturator reline, speech, swallowing and dental care; varenicline at full dose
Six-week review: smoking down by two thirds, setting a quit date, pain and weight
Twelve-week review: five weeks without smoking, the new obturator and survivorship surveillance
Five-month review: abstinence, lung and aortic screening results, pain, weight and the survivorship plan
Same-day sick visit for Candida stomatitis under the obturator

Tobacco: a nonjudgmental assessment of readiness and of what cigars do for him; varenicline started now, before a quit date, with a plan to cut down and then stop; combination nicotine replacement (patch and lozenge) added from the quit date; cigars are counted like any other tobacco; weekly behavioral support by phone with the national quitline and in clinic; relapse treated as part of the process
Maxillofacial prosthodontics consultation for a worn, poorly sealing obturator with pain, hypernasal speech and nasal leakage, and for dental care

Head and neck cancer survivorship: yearly examination of the mouth, defect and neck by his head and neck surgeon (more than five years after treatment), self-examination of the mouth, prompt review of any sore, lump, bleeding or change that lasts two weeks, imaging only for symptoms, and counseling on the risk of second primary cancers of the mouth, throat, larynx, esophagus and lung, which stopping smoking lowers
Chronic pain: scheduled acetaminophen up to 3,000 mg a day, a well-fitting obturator, warm saline rinses, and no long-term opioids; the plan is reviewed at each visit with a pain score
Nutrition: dietitian advice on soft high-protein meals, oral nutrition supplements twice daily, weight at each visit and albumin rechecked

Prosthodontic care: chairside reline and flange adjustment now, a new definitive obturator, nightly cleaning and an overnight soak, high-fluoride toothpaste, dental cleaning every three months, nicotine lozenge rather than gum, and speech and swallowing therapy sessions with a speech-language pathologist after the reline
Cardiovascular risk: lipid panel and 10-year risk estimate; a statin discussed with him once the smoking plan is under way
Stop smoking cigars completely, at a pace he chooses, using varenicline and nicotine replacement
Twenty cigars a day to six by six weeks; no smoking since the quit date apart from one cigar in the second week; about fourteen weeks without smoking at five months
An obturator that seals and does not rub, so that speech is clear and liquids do not leak into his nose
Reline at two weeks; new definitive obturator fitted at twelve weeks; speech clear and no nasal leakage
Pain at 3 of 10 or less without opioids
Pain 6 to 2 of 10 on scheduled acetaminophen with a well-fitting obturator
Regain weight to at least 60 kg with a normal albumin
Weight 58.4 to 60.6 kg; albumin 3.4 to 3.9 g/dL
